## clean_names_lowercase function
```{r Load clean_names_lowercase function}
# Takes text and standardizes it, which we will need for merging later on:

clean_names_lowercase <- function(x) {

  x <- iconv(x, from = "", to = "UTF-8", sub = "")
  x <- stringi::stri_trans_general(x, "Latin-ASCII")

  x %>%
    tolower() %>%
    trimws()
}
```

## clean_names function
```{r Load clean_names function}
# Takes text and standardizes it, which we will need for merging later on:

clean_names <- function(x) {

  x <- iconv(x, from = "", to = "UTF-8", sub = "")
  x <- stringi::stri_trans_general(x, "Latin-ASCII")

  x %>%
    toupper() %>%
    trimws() %>%
    gsub("\\bDE\\b", "", .) %>%
    gsub("\\s*\\([^\\)]*\\)", "", .) %>%   # remove parentheses + contents
    gsub("\\s+", " ", .) %>%
    trimws()
}
```

```{r Filter out keywords from recorded_taxa_name to get recorded_taxa_name_clean}

# PART A. Keyword list [SUBJECT TO EDITS] -----------------

# NOTE: Keyword list excludes "ALETA" which is handled separately.

Keyword_list <- c(
# Processing state or product form (e.g., frozen, full fish, filleted, beheaded, dried, etc.):
  "S.C.", "S/C", "S",
  "FRESCO", "FRESCA", "FCA", "FCO", "FC",
  "ECO",
  "CONG", "CONGELADO",
  "SECO DE", "SECA", "SECA DE", "SECO", "SECO DE",
  "COCINERO", "COCIDO", "COCIDA", "COCIDAS", "ASADO",
  "ENTERO", "ENTERA", "IND", "ENT",
  "FILETE", "FILETE DE", "ECA", "FILETE DE ECO", "DESHUESADA", "CARNE", "CARNE DE",
  "DESCABEZADO", "DES", "DSC", "DESC", "DESV", "DESVICERADO",

# Animal parts:
  "MANTO", "MANTO DE",
  "PULPA DE", "PULPA FRESCA",
  "POLVO DE",
  "TENTACULOS DE", "TUBO DE", "TUBO",
  "CABEZA DE", "BUCHE", "BUCHE DE", "TRIPA DE", "COLAS DE", "MANOS DE", "MANOS",
  "ANCAS DE", "ANCAS", "ANCA",
  "PIEL DE ECA", "PIEL DE SECA", "PIEL DE", "PIEL",

# Remove ALETA from main keywords; we'll handle these keywords separately:
  #"ALETA", "ALETA ECA DE", "ALETA FCA DE"

# Shells and pearls:
  "CONCHA NACAR", "CONCHA DE",
  "PERLAS", "MEDIAS PERLAS",

# From where / habitat type:
  "DE ALTA MAR",
  "DE AGUA DULCE",

# Live culture or cultivation techniques:
  "VIVO", "VIVA", "VIVAS", "VIVITA",
  "DE CULTIVO", "DE CULTIVO VIVO", 
  "CULTIVADA", "CULTIVADO", "CULTIVADAS", "CULTIVADOS", # A few new adds as of May 04
  "ABASTO RANCHO", "RANCHO",

# Eggs:
  "HUEVA DE",

# Used as bait:
  "CARNADA", "P/CARNADA",

# Other:
  "NO APTO PARA EMPAQUE"
)

# 79 keywords as of Mar 23 2026.

# Order the key words longest first (note that this is necessary for the next steps):
Keyword_list <- Keyword_list[order(nchar(Keyword_list), 
                                   decreasing = TRUE)]

# Escape regex meta-characters:
Keyword_list_escaped <- stringi::stri_replace_all_regex(
  Keyword_list, 
  "([.|(){}+*?^$\\[\\]\\\\])", 
  "\\\\$1"
)

# Final regex:
Keyword_pattern <- paste0(
  "(?<![A-Za-z0-9])(",
  paste(Keyword_list_escaped, collapse = "|"),
  ")(?![A-Za-z0-9])"
)


# PART B. Flag special "ALETA" phrases (handled differently from other key words) -----------------

# Lookahead function:
build_de_pattern <- function(word, exclusions = NULL) {
  base <- paste0("\\b", word, "\\b")
  
  if (!is.null(exclusions)) {
    base <- paste0(
      base,
      "(?!\\s+(?:", paste(exclusions, collapse = "|"), "))"
    )
  }
  
  paste0(base, "\\s*(?:DE)?")
}

# Look-behind function (for OSTION DE ROCA)
build_de_pattern_behind <- function(word, exclusions = NULL) {
  base <- paste0("\\b", word, "\\b")

  if (!is.null(exclusions)) {
    base <- paste0(
      "(?<!\\b(?:", paste(exclusions, collapse = "|"), ")\\s)",
      base
    )
  }

  paste0(base, "(?:\\s+DE)?")
}

de_keywords <- c("ALETA", "FILETE", "CARNE", "COLA", "ROCA")

# Lookahead exclusions: words following the keyword
special_aleta_cases <- c(
  "BLANCA", "AMARILLA", "CORTA", "AZUL", "CARTON"
)

aleta_pattern <- build_de_pattern(
  "ALETA", special_aleta_cases
)

cabeza_pattern <- build_de_pattern(
  "CABEZA", c("GIGANTE")
)

# Lookbehind exclusions: words preceding the keyword
roca_pattern <- build_de_pattern_behind(
  "ROCA", c("OSTION DE")
)

# Special case for Almeja Concha Espina
concha_pattern <- paste0(
  "(?<!\\bALMEJA\\s)",
  "\\bCONCHA\\b",
  "(?!\\s+ESPINA)",
  "(?:\\s+DE)?"
)

# No exclusions (as of now)
filete_pattern <- build_de_pattern("FILETE")
carne_pattern  <- build_de_pattern("CARNE")
cola_pattern   <- build_de_pattern("COLA")

Keyword_pattern <- paste0(
  "(?<![A-Za-z0-9])(",
  paste(
    c(
      aleta_pattern,
      filete_pattern,
      carne_pattern,
      cola_pattern,
      roca_pattern,
      cabeza_pattern,

      # Specific phrase must precede the general CONCHA pattern
      Keyword_list_escaped[Keyword_list == "CONCHA NACAR"],

      concha_pattern,
      Keyword_list_escaped[
        Keyword_list != "CONCHA NACAR"
      ]
    ),
    collapse = "|"
  ),
  ")(?![A-Za-z0-9])"
)

I think I started out with some preliminary version of the separate, parse functionality, quickly spotted the beginnings of a keywords list and then grew the list over time. Come back to this at some point to recreate this early part of the workflow to document it (reproducibility).
```

```{r Protect special DE phrases}

# Phrases where "DE" must be preserved
protected_de_phrases <- c(
  "PEPINO DE MAR",
  "OSTION DE ROCA"
)

# Placeholder for spaces within protected phrases
de_placeholder <- "ZZZ_protected_ZZZ"

# Protect phrases before keyword removal
protect_de_phrases <- function(x, phrases) {
  for (phrase in phrases) {
    protected <- stringi::stri_replace_all_fixed(
      phrase,
      " ",
      de_placeholder
    )

    x <- stringi::stri_replace_all_fixed(
      x,
      phrase,
      protected,
      opts_fixed = list(case_insensitive = TRUE)
    )
  }

  x
}

# Restore protected phrases after cleaning
restore_de_phrases <- function(x) {
  stringi::stri_replace_all_fixed(
    x,
    de_placeholder,
    " "
  )
}
```

# STEP 3b: Separate out keywords from the original landing record using the parse regex in PART C:

```{r Separate keywords from landing record based on parse function}
# PART C. MAIN PARSING PIPELINE -----------------
# RUN TIME= 6-8 min, optimized but still computationally heavy

# TRY NEW
Mex.Pacific_Landings_parsed <- Mex.Pacific_Landings %>%

  # Rename columns
  rename(
    recorded_taxa_name = species_name,
    recorded_taxa_group = main_species_group
  ) %>%

  # Extract scientific name before cleaning
  mutate(
    recorded_scientific_name =
      stringi::stri_extract_first_regex(
        recorded_taxa_name,
        "\\(([^)]+)\\)"
      ) %>%
      stringi::stri_replace_all_regex("\\(|\\)", ""),

    scientific_name_recorded_T.F =
      !is.na(recorded_scientific_name),

    recorded_scientific_name = if_else(
      scientific_name_recorded_T.F,
      stringi::stri_trans_totitle(recorded_scientific_name),
      NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%

  # Extract keywords from the original recorded name
  mutate(
    keywords_list = stringi::stri_extract_all_regex(
      recorded_taxa_name,
      Keyword_pattern
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    keywords_list = map(
      keywords_list,
      ~ {
        length(.x) <- 5
        .x
      }
    )
  ) %>%
  unnest_wider(
    keywords_list,
    names_sep = "_"
  ) %>%
  rename_with(
    ~ paste0("keywords_", 1:5),
    starts_with("keywords_list_")
  ) %>%

  # Clean recorded_taxa_name
  mutate(
    recorded_taxa_name_clean = recorded_taxa_name %>%

      # Protect meaningful phrases BEFORE keyword removal
      protect_de_phrases(protected_de_phrases) %>%

      # Remove other keywords
      stringi::stri_replace_all_regex(
        Keyword_pattern,
        ""
      ) %>%

      # Remove standalone modifiers Y / DE,
      # except DE after ALETA
      stringi::stri_replace_all_regex(
        "(?<!ALETA\\s)\\bDE\\b|\\bY\\b",
        ""
      ) %>%

      # Remove P/ or P /
      stringi::stri_replace_all_regex(
        "\\bP\\s*/\\s*",
        ""
      ) %>%

      # Remove punctuation
      stringi::stri_replace_all_regex(
        "[.,/\\\\]+",
        " "
      ) %>%

      # Normalize whitespace
      stringi::stri_replace_all_regex(
        "\\s+",
        " "
      ) %>%
      stringr::str_squish() %>%

      # Restore protected phrases
      restore_de_phrases()
  ) %>%

  # Extract common name
  mutate(
    common_name_clean = stringi::stri_trim_both(
      stringi::stri_replace_first_regex(
        recorded_taxa_name_clean,
        "\\s*\\([^)]*\\)",
        ""
      )
    ),
    common_name_clean = tolower(common_name_clean)
  )

dim(Mex.Pacific_Landings_parsed)
# 6684642 obs., 30 vars.

# PART D. Trim and reorder columns -----------------
colnames(Mex.Pacific_Landings_parsed)

Mex.Pacific_Landings_parsed <- Mex.Pacific_Landings_parsed %>%

  select(
    # General info from record:
    state, office_name, landing_site, landing_site_key,
    year, month,
    receipt_date_fixed, period_start_fixed, period_end_fixed,
    fleet, acuaculture_production, eu_rnpa, eu_name, vessel_rnpa, vessel_name,
    
    # Species info from record:
    recorded_taxa_group, recorded_taxa_name,
    
    # Cleaned and derived names:
    recorded_taxa_name_clean, recorded_scientific_name,
    scientific_name_recorded_T.F, common_name_clean,
    
    # Keywords that have been parsed:
    keywords_1, keywords_2, keywords_3, keywords_4, keywords_5,
    
    # Landing details from record:
    value, landed_weight, live_weight, weight_kg_corrected
 
  )
# 6684642 obs., 30 vars.

# How many common names are there in this data frame?
length(unique(Mex.Pacific_Landings_parsed$common_name_clean))
length(unique(Mex.Pacific_Landings_parsed$recorded_taxa_group))
# NOW 921 common names (up from 732 when only the GOC), over 58 taxonomic groups
```

```{r SANITY CHECK 2: Investigating Keywords}
# Longest-first ordering in the regex ensures: multi-word phrases match fully BEFORE matching component words.
# Component words will not appear separately in the extraction. So, for example, "VIVO P/ABASTO RANCHO" gets abstracted as "VIVO" and "ABASTO RANCHO" before "RANCHO" can be extracted.
# >> This is why my unique keyword vector has fewer elements than your list of 81 — some keywords are never extracted as standalone because they are covered by longer matches.
```

# PATCH 3 - Fix major taxonomic groups (Oct 2026)

```{r Complicated merge landings data with MajorGroupKey_pending}
SPECIAL_GROUPS <- c("OTRAS", "ESPECIE GENERICA", "FAUNA", "ORNATO", "PECES DE ORNATO", "NEI")

#STEP 1: Join in non-OTRAS, simple join
# For non-otra taxa, we only want to look up based on the recorded_taxa_group and estimated_genus_name. From that look-up we want to assign Major_Functional_Group, Assignment_for_Major_Functional_Group
NONOTRAS_MajorGroupKey_lookup <- MajorGroupKey_pending %>%
  filter(!recorded_taxa_group %in% SPECIAL_GROUPS) %>%
  select(-c("common_name_clean", "IHH_functional_major_groups_sm", "estimated_species_name", "Manual_Classification_Notes", "species_est_certainty", "species_est_reasoning", "genus_est_reasoning", "ornamentalFLAG_1")) %>%
  distinct(
    recorded_taxa_group,
    estimated_genus_name,
    .keep_all = TRUE
  )

# 219 obs. 5 vars.
  
join_NormalGroups <- Mex.Pacific_Landings_species %>%
  filter(!recorded_taxa_group %in% SPECIAL_GROUPS) %>%
  left_join(
    NONOTRAS_MajorGroupKey_lookup,
    by = c("recorded_taxa_group","estimated_genus_name")
  )
# 570513 obs. (the majority of the data, as expected) and 41 vars (+3 new vars).

# SANITY CHECK
subset<- join_NormalGroups %>% filter(is.na(Major_Functional_Group))
table(subset$recorded_taxa_group)
# Relatively small number (n= 7620, 1% of join_NormalGroups), pretty good!

# STEP 2: JOIN IN OTRAS
# In contrast: for otras taxa, we want to look up based on the recorded_taxa_group and common_name_clean. From that look-up we want to assign estimated_taxa_group, estimated_species_name, species_est_certainty, species_est_reasoning, estimated_genus_name, genus_est_reasoning, Major_Functional_Group, Assignment_for_Major_Functional_Group, Manual_Classification_Notes, and ornamentalFLAG_1
OTRAS_MajorGroupKey_lookup <- MajorGroupKey_pending %>%
  filter(recorded_taxa_group %in% SPECIAL_GROUPS) %>%
  distinct(
    recorded_taxa_group,
    common_name_clean,
    .keep_all = TRUE
  )
# 278 obs. 13 vars.

join_SpecialGroups <- Mex.Pacific_Landings_species %>%
  filter(recorded_taxa_group %in% SPECIAL_GROUPS) %>%
  left_join(
    OTRAS_MajorGroupKey_lookup,
    by = c("recorded_taxa_group", "common_name_clean"),
    suffix = c("", "_new")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      ends_with("_new"),
      ~ .,
      .names = "{sub('_new$', '', .col)}"
    )
  )

join_SpecialGroups <- join_SpecialGroups %>%
  select(-ends_with("_new"))

# 979489 obs. (as expected) and 45 vars. (+7 new vars).

# STEP 3:
Mex.Pacific_Landings_classed0 <- bind_rows(join_NormalGroups, join_SpecialGroups)
# 6684642 obs. (as expected) and 45 vars.
```

# PATCH 5 - Most likely family
```{r Patch the family column}
TEST<- Mex.Pacific_Landings_classed0 %>%
    slice_sample(n = 1000)

# Missing, unknown, or "NEI" in estimated_family_name
sum(
  is.na(Mex.Pacific_Landings_classed0$estimated_family_name) |
  tolower(trimws(Mex.Pacific_Landings_classed0$estimated_family_name)) %in% c("nei", "unknown"),
  na.rm = TRUE
)
# 851570 records

# Missing, unknown, or "NEI" in most_likely_family
sum(
  is.na(Mex.Pacific_Landings_classed0$most_likely_family) |
  tolower(trimws(Mex.Pacific_Landings_classed0$most_likely_family)) %in% c("nei", "unknown"),
  na.rm = TRUE
)
# 454417 records

# Where do these columns differ?
head(
  Mex.Pacific_Landings_classed0[
    tolower(Mex.Pacific_Landings_classed0$estimated_family_name) !=
      tolower(Mex.Pacific_Landings_classed0$most_likely_family) |
    is.na(Mex.Pacific_Landings_classed0$estimated_family_name) !=
      is.na(Mex.Pacific_Landings_classed0$most_likely_family),
    c("estimated_family_name", "most_likely_family")
  ],
  20
)

# Over-ride estimated_family_name with most_likely_family as applicable:
Mex.Pacific_Landings_classed0 <- Mex.Pacific_Landings_classed0 %>%
  mutate(
    family_name_checked = if_else(
      !is.na(most_likely_family) &
        (is.na(estimated_family_name) |
         tolower(estimated_family_name) != tolower(most_likely_family)),
      most_likely_family,
      estimated_family_name
    )
  )

# Check to see if it worked:
Mex.Pacific_Landings_classed0 %>%
  filter(
    is.na(estimated_family_name) != is.na(family_name_checked) |
      (!is.na(estimated_family_name) &
       !is.na(family_name_checked) &
       tolower(estimated_family_name) != tolower(family_name_checked))
  ) %>%
  select(estimated_family_name, most_likely_family, family_name_checked) %>%
  slice_head(n = 50)

```

# > SHIFTING GEARS: Estimate sector ------------------------------

# > STEP 7: FLAG and estimate landings from AQUACULTURE based on a series of logical rules.
I think aquaculture and mariculture in the region is being vastly under-counted and under-reported.
Let's implement a series of rules to estimate if records are associated with aquaculture or not.

```{r Load in dataframe as needed}

dim(Mex.Pacific_Landings_classed)
```

## STEP 7a: FLAG AQUACULTURE:

```{r Create a Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0 dataframe}

Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0$est_aquaculture_production<- c(NA)
# 6684642 obs., 45 vars.
```

VIEW: ALL KEY WORDS
```{r Investigating Keywords}
# Extract all unique keywords from keyword columns 1 through 5. Delete exact duplicates. 
Keyword_vector <- Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0 %>%
  select(keywords_1:keywords_5) %>%
  unlist() %>%
  unique() %>%
  na.omit()

Keyword_vector
```

First, let's flag landing_site names and eu_name that are associated with aquaculture.
```{r Estimate likelihood of aquaculture based on name of landing_site and eu_name}
#### FLAG 1 - Flag aquaculture based on landing_site and eu_name (3 levels: YES, NO, POSSIBLY): ####

# Clues from landing_site and eu_name
LandingSite_strong.clues<- c("CULTIVADORES", "ESTANQUE", "VIVEROS", "ACUACULTURA") 

LandingSite_clues<- c("CULT", "DREN", "BORDO", "PREDIO")

EUname_clues<- c("ACUICOLA", "FARMS", "MARICULTURA",
                        "MARICULTIVOS",
                        "AGROACUICOLA", "AGRICOLA",
                        "ACUACULTURA", "AQUACULTURE",
                        "GRANJA", "GRANJA CAMARONERA",
                        "RANCHO")

# Build regex patterns dynamically
LandingSite_strong_pattern <- paste0("\\b(", paste(LandingSite_strong.clues, collapse = "|"), ")\\b")
LandingSite_weak_pattern <- paste0("\\b(", paste(LandingSite_clues, collapse = "|"), ")\\b")
EUname_pattern <- paste0("\\b(", paste(EUname_clues, collapse = "|"), ")\\b")

Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0 <- Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0 %>%
  
  mutate(
    acuaculture_production_norm = str_to_lower(str_trim(acuaculture_production))
  ) %>%
  
  mutate(
    aquacultureFLAG_site.details = case_when(
      str_detect(landing_site, regex(LandingSite_strong_pattern, ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "YES",
      str_detect(landing_site, regex(LandingSite_weak_pattern, ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "POSSIBLY",
      str_detect(eu_name, regex(EUname_pattern, ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "POSSIBLY",
      TRUE ~ "NO"
    )
  ) %>%
  
  select(-acuaculture_production_norm)

# SANITY CHECK:
# Check that we pulled out landing sites that make sense:
table(Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0$aquacultureFLAG_site.details)

 #      NO POSSIBLY      YES 
 # 6488719   195385      538 

# Take a closer look at the possible and yes aquaculture sites:
subset<- Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0 %>%
  filter(aquacultureFLAG_site.details %in% c(
    "YES",
    "POSSIBLY"
  )) %>%
  distinct(landing_site, eu_name, aquacultureFLAG_site.details) %>%
  arrange(landing_site, eu_name)

# 1885 sites 
# Most all make sense to me! If an organism came from one of these sites I would assume it was a farmed species, even if the record was NOT marked as aquaculture.
```

```{r Flagging aquaculture landings based on key words}
  "ABASTO RANCHO", "RANCHO", "PERLAS", "MEDIAS PERLAS"
```

Next, let's implement rules based on taxa. What taxa are likely aquaculture?
```{r Flag certain aquaculture and NOT-aquaculture taxa}
#### FLAG 3 - Flag known, likely, and NOT aquaculture taxa [LIST IS SUBJECT TO CHANGE] ####
# In theory, there could be clues in a number of columns: estimated_taxa_group, recorded_taxa_group, recorded_taxa_name, common_name_clean

table(Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0$estimated_taxa_group)
table(Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0$common_name_clean)

DEFINITE_AQUA.TAXA <- c("TILAPIA") # common_name_clean
UNLIKELY_AQUA.CLASS <- c("Anchovy & Sardine (small pelagics)", "Cephalopods", "Echinoderms") # Major_Functional_Group

Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0 <- Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0 %>%
  mutate(
    aquacultureFLAG_specific.taxa = case_when(
      str_to_upper(str_trim(common_name_clean)) %in% DEFINITE_AQUA.TAXA ~ "YES",
      str_to_upper(str_trim(estimated_taxa_group)) %in% POSSIBLE_AQUA.GROUP ~ "POSSIBLY",
      str_trim(Major_Functional_Group) %in% UNLIKELY_AQUA.CLASS ~ "PROBABLY NOT",
      TRUE ~ "NO"
    )
  )

table(Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0$aquacultureFLAG_specific.taxa)
```

Flag what CANNOT be aquaculture based on what we know about the taxa's natural history:
```{r Flag Major_Functional_Groups that are definitely NOT aquaculture like sharks}
#### FLAG 4 - Flag Major_Functional_Groups that are DEFINITELY not aquaculture [LIST IS SUBJECT TO CHANGE] ####

table(Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0$estimated_taxa_group)
table(Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0$Major_Functional_Group)

# DEFINITELY NOT:
NOT_AQUA.CLASS <- c("Jellies", "Sharks") # Major_Functional_Groups
NOT_AQUA.GENERA <- c("Istiophorus", "Makaira", "Tetrapturus", "Xiphias", "Acanthocybium", "Dosidicus") # estimated_genus_name

Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0 <- Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0 %>%
  mutate(
    NOTaquacultureFLAG_specific.groups = case_when(
      str_trim(Major_Functional_Group) %in% NOT_AQUA.CLASS ~ "CANNOT BE AQUACULTURE",
      str_trim(estimated_genus_name) %in% NOT_AQUA.GENERA ~ "CANNOT BE AQUACULTURE",
      TRUE ~ NA
    )
  )

table(Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0$NOTaquacultureFLAG_specific.groups)

# CANNOT BE AQUACULTURE 
#                428905

# For the entire Mexican Pacific (May 04 2026):
# CANNOT BE AQUACULTURE 
#                409569
```

Create a combined aquaculture flag based on the previous three flags (aquacultureFLAG_site.details, aquacultureFLAG_keywords, aquacultureFLAG_specific.taxa) and the new flag NOTaquacultureFLAG_specific.groups

Here's the logic for the combined flag:

• If at least one flag is "YES", then flags indicate that aquaculture is highly likely and aquacultureFLAG_combined = "YES" (my YES flags are pretty robust at this point)
• If one more flags is "POSSIBLY", then aquacultureFLAG_combined is "possibly aquaculture" but not certain
• If no flags indicate aquaculture, then aquacultureFLAG_combined is "NO"

• BUT, if the NOTaquacultureFLAG_specific.groups indicates CANNOT BE AQUACULTURE, then combined flag is "NO"


```{r Create a combined aquaculture flag}
#### FLAG 5 - Create a combined aquaculture flag based on the previous four flags ####
Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0 <- Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0 %>%
  
  # Remember, put the strongest condition first:
  mutate(
    aquacultureFLAG_combined = case_when(
      
      if_any(c(NOTaquacultureFLAG_specific.groups), ~ .x == "CANNOT BE AQUACULTURE") ~ "CANNOT BE AQUACULTURE",
      
      if_any(c(aquacultureFLAG_specific.taxa), ~ .x == "PROBABLY NOT") ~ "PROBABLY NOT",
      
      if_any(c(aquacultureFLAG_site.details,
               aquacultureFLAG_keywords,
               aquacultureFLAG_specific.taxa), ~ .x == "YES") ~ "YES",
      
      if_any(c(aquacultureFLAG_site.details,
               aquacultureFLAG_keywords,
               aquacultureFLAG_specific.taxa), ~ .x == "POSSIBLY") ~ "POSSIBLY",
      
      TRUE ~ "NO"
    )
  )

# SANITY CHECK: Is there disagreement between the flags?
subset<- Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0 %>% 
  filter(aquacultureFLAG_site.details %in% c("YES", "POSSIBLY") & 
           aquacultureFLAG_combined=="CANNOT BE AQUACULTURE")

table(subset$estimated_taxa_group)
# There are 9469 where site names / details are incongruous with the taxa being caught. 
# For example, giant squid and sharks are not used for aquaculture: maybe these are taxa ASSOCIATED with aquaculture, or found new aquaculture sites but not actually aquaculture?

# Good! This shows that our aquacultureFLAG_combined is working, trumping other flags.

```

## STEP 7b: ESTIMATE AQUACULTURE:
Here is the logic and set of decisions designed to estimate aquaculture:

Decision Table:
Report      aquacultureFLAG_combined  aquaculture_estimate    certainty
  yes       YES                       aquaculture             high; aquaculture flags agree with original report
  yes       POSSIBLY                  aquaculture             high; aquaculture flags agree with original report
  yes       NO                        aquaculture	            medium; no flags for aquaculture but original report says aquaculture
  yes       PROBABLY NOT              possibly aquaculture    low; aquaculture flags do not agree with original report
  yes       CANNOT BE AQUACULTURE     not aquaculture         medium; aquaculture flags suggest cannot be aquaculture, original report likely wrong
  
  no        YES	                      likely aquaculture	    medium; flags suggest aquaculture but original report says no, report could be wrong
  no        POSSIBLY                  possibly aquaculture    low; flags suggest possibly aquaculture but original report says no
  no        NO                        not aquaculture         high; aquaculture flags agree with original report
  no        PROBABLY NOT              not aquaculture         high; aquaculture flags agree with original report
  no        CANNOT BE AQUACULTURE     not aquaculture         high; aquaculture flags agree with original report
  
  NA        YES                       likely aquaculture      medium; no data from original report but flags suggest most likely aquaculture
  NA        POSSIBLY                  possibly aquaculture    low; no data from original report but flags suggest possibly aquaculture
  NA        NO                        unlikely aquaculture    medium; no data from original report and flags do not suggest aquaculture
  NA        PROBABLY NOT              unlikely aquaculture    high; no data from original report and flags suggest probably not aquaculture
  NA        CANNOT BE AQUACULTURE     not aquaculture         high; no data from original report and flags suggest definitely not aquaculture

```{r Generate estimates and confidence values}
#### Estimate aquaculture and confidence values based on the comparison of aquacultureFLAG_combined versus the official report: ####
Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0 <- Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0 %>%
  mutate(
    # Normalize original report:
    acuaculture_original.report = str_to_lower(str_trim(acuaculture_production)),

    # ESTIMATE OF AQUACULTURE:
    est_aquaculture_production = case_when(
      
      # Report = YES
      acuaculture_original.report == "yes" & aquacultureFLAG_combined %in% c("YES", "POSSIBLY", "NO") ~ "aquaculture",
      acuaculture_original.report == "yes" & aquacultureFLAG_combined == "PROBABLY NOT" ~ "possibly aquaculture",
      acuaculture_original.report == "yes" & aquacultureFLAG_combined == "CANNOT BE AQUACULTURE" ~ "not aquaculture",
      
      # Report = NO
      acuaculture_original.report == "no" & aquacultureFLAG_combined == "YES" ~ "likely aquaculture",
      acuaculture_original.report == "no" & aquacultureFLAG_combined == "POSSIBLY" ~ "possibly aquaculture",
      acuaculture_original.report == "no" & aquacultureFLAG_combined %in% c("NO", "PROBABLY NOT", "CANNOT BE AQUACULTURE") ~ "not aquaculture",
      
      # Report = NA
      is.na(acuaculture_original.report) & aquacultureFLAG_combined == "YES" ~ "likely aquaculture",
      is.na(acuaculture_original.report) & aquacultureFLAG_combined == "POSSIBLY" ~ "possibly aquaculture",
      is.na(acuaculture_original.report) & aquacultureFLAG_combined == "NO" ~ "unlikely aquaculture",
      is.na(acuaculture_original.report) & aquacultureFLAG_combined == "PROBABLY NOT" ~ "unlikely aquaculture",
      is.na(acuaculture_original.report) & aquacultureFLAG_combined == "CANNOT BE AQUACULTURE" ~ "not aquaculture",
      
      TRUE ~ "uncertain"
    ),

    # CERTAINTY ESTIMATES:
    est_aquaculture_certainty = case_when(
      
      # Report = YES
      acuaculture_original.report == "yes" & aquacultureFLAG_combined %in% c("YES", "POSSIBLY") ~ "high; aquaculture flags agree with original report",
      acuaculture_original.report == "yes" & aquacultureFLAG_combined == "NO" ~ "medium; no flags for aquaculture but original report says aquaculture",
      acuaculture_original.report == "yes" & aquacultureFLAG_combined == "PROBABLY NOT" ~ "low; aquaculture flags do not agree with original report",
      acuaculture_original.report == "yes" & aquacultureFLAG_combined == "CANNOT BE AQUACULTURE" ~ "medium; aquaculture flags suggest cannot be aquaculture, original report likely wrong",
      
      # Report = NO
      acuaculture_original.report == "no" & aquacultureFLAG_combined == "YES" ~ "medium; flags suggest aquaculture but original report says no, report could be wrong",
      acuaculture_original.report == "no" & aquacultureFLAG_combined == "POSSIBLY" ~ "low; flags suggest possibly aquaculture but original report says no",
      acuaculture_original.report == "no" & aquacultureFLAG_combined %in% c("NO", "PROBABLY NOT", "CANNOT BE AQUACULTURE") ~ "high; aquaculture flags agree with original report",
      
      # Report = NA
      is.na(acuaculture_original.report) & aquacultureFLAG_combined == "YES" ~ "medium; no data from original report but flags suggest most likely aquaculture",
      is.na(acuaculture_original.report) & aquacultureFLAG_combined == "POSSIBLY" ~ "low; no data from original report but flags suggest possibly aquaculture",
      is.na(acuaculture_original.report) & aquacultureFLAG_combined == "NO" ~ "medium; no data from original report and flags do not suggest aquaculture",
      is.na(acuaculture_original.report) & aquacultureFLAG_combined == "PROBABLY NOT" ~ "high; no data from original report and flags suggest probably not aquaculture",
      is.na(acuaculture_original.report) & aquacultureFLAG_combined == "CANNOT BE AQUACULTURE" ~ "high; no data from original report and flags suggest definitely not aquaculture",
      
      TRUE ~ "not enough information to assign aquaculture estimate"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-acuaculture_original.report)

dim(Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0)
# 6684642 obs., 51 vars.
```

Notice the spike in landings from 2017-2018? Of course, how could you miss it.
This jump coincides with a change in reporting associated with the raw data itself. 
Data pre-2018 is reported here: mex_conapesca_avisos_2000_2019.rds
Data 2018 and onward is reported here: mex_conapesca_apertura_2018_present.rds

# > STEP 8: FLAG and estimate landings from FRESHWATER based on a series of logical rules. ------------------------------
```{r Flag freshwater landings}
table(Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0$Major_Functional_Group)

# Possible freshwater fishes:
subset<- Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0 %>%
  filter(Major_Functional_Group== "Diadromous fishes")

table(subset$estimated_genus_name)
# Makes sense: Anguilla and Chanos

#### FLAG 1 - Flag freshwater based on keywords, FRESHWATER_KEYWORDS [LIST IS SUBJECT TO CHANGE] ####

FRESHWATER_KEYWORDS<- c(
  "DE AGUA DULCE"
)

#### FLAG 2 - Flag freshwater based on key taxa, KNOWN_FRESHWATER_TAXA [LIST IS SUBJECT TO CHANGE] ####
KNOWN_FRESHWATER_TAXA<- c(
  "tilapia",
  "rana", "rana toro",
  "trucha",
  "bagre canal"
) #common_name_clean

#### FLAG 3 - Flag known freshwater or marine genera [LIST IS SUBJECT TO CHANGE] ####
KNOWN_FRESHWATER_GENERA<- c(
  "Cyprinus", # common carp; strictly freshwater.
  "Macrobrachium", # freshwater prawns/shrimps; mostly freshwater.
  "Hypophthalmichthys", # Asian carp; freshwater.
  "Chirostoma", # “charales,” endemic to freshwater lakes in Mexico.
  "Carassius", # goldfish/crucian carp; freshwater.
  "Micropterus", # black bass; freshwater.
  "Lepomis", # sunfish; freshwater.
  "Cyprinodon", # pupfish; freshwater.
  "Rana" # frogs
  ) # estimated_genus_name

KNOWN_MARINE_GENERA<- c("Penaeus") # New add as of May 04 2026

#### FLAG 4 & 5 - Flag freshwater versus NOT based on Major_Functional_Group and est_habitat type [LIST IS SUBJECT TO CHANGE] ####

# Flag freshwater rows based on keywords (FLAGS 6 and 7), info from the IHH key, and estimated habitat type (based on landing site):
table(Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0$Major_Functional_Group)

# Definitely freshwater:
KNOWN_FRESHWATER_CLASSES<- c("Freshwater fishes", "Other freshwater taxa")

# Could be freshwater or marine:
UNKNOWN_MAR.FRESHWATER_CLASSES<- c("Marine or freshwater fishes NEI", "unknown")

# More likely to be marine:
LIKELY_MARINE_CLASSES<- c("Diadromous fishes", "Molluscs excl. Cephalopods", "Shrimps, prawns")

# Definitely marine:
KNOWN_MARINE_CLASSES<- c("Anchovy & Sardine (small pelagics)", "Cephalopods", "Crustaceans", "Demersal marine fishes", "Echinoderms", "Jellies", "Marine algae", "Marine fishes NEI", "Marine species NEI", "Other marine invertebrates", "Pelagic marine fish (excl. anchovy & sardine)", "Sharks")
# - Crustaceans could technically be split but are overwhelmingly marine.
# - Molluscs could technically be split but are overwhelmingly marine. There could be some freshwater clams hiding in there.
# - Shrimp technically split but overwhelmingly marine. When in doubt, lean marine.

  
# Logic:
# - First, any row whose functional group is explicitly in KNOWN_MARINE_CLASSES will immediately get "CANNOT BE FRESHWATER; MARINE"
# - Second, if a row didn’t hit the first condition, it is evaluated for strong freshwater evidence. "YES FRESHWATER"
# - Third, rows that didn’t match the first two conditions are considered. This is broader marine signal. "LIKELY MARINE"
# - Fourth, rows that didn’t match the first two conditions are considered. This is an uncertain signal. "POSSIBLY FRESHWATER OR MARINE"
# - Finally, Any row that didn’t meet any of the above conditions gets "NOT FLAGGED EITHER WAY".

Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0 <- Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0 %>%
  mutate(
    freshwater_flag = case_when(

      # Definitely NOT freshwater:
      (Major_Functional_Group %in% KNOWN_MARINE_CLASSES) |
      (estimated_genus_name %in% KNOWN_MARINE_GENERA) ~
        "CANNOT BE FRESHWATER; DEFINITE MARINE",

      # Definite freshwater: any definite criteria
      (Major_Functional_Group %in% KNOWN_FRESHWATER_CLASSES) |
      (common_name_clean %in% KNOWN_FRESHWATER_TAXA) |
      (estimated_genus_name %in% KNOWN_FRESHWATER_GENERA) |
      (rowSums(
        across(keywords_1:keywords_5,
               ~ .x %in% FRESHWATER_KEYWORDS),
        na.rm = TRUE
      ) > 0) ~ "DEFINITE FRESHWATER",

      # Likely marine: broader/uncertain criteria
      (Major_Functional_Group %in% LIKELY_MARINE_CLASSES) ~
        "LIKELY MARINE",

      # Possible freshwater or marine
      (Major_Functional_Group %in% UNKNOWN_MAR.FRESHWATER_CLASSES) ~
        "POSSIBLY FRESHWATER OR MARINE",

      # Otherwise
      TRUE ~ "NOT FLAGGED EITHER WAY"
    )
  )

table(Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted0$freshwater_flag)
# 671082 observations flagged as YES definitely "freshwater" based on: freshwater keywords, the taxa common name, landing site, or Major_Functional_Group. Meanwhile, other entries, like "MOJARRA" could go either way and are flagged as possibly freshwater.

# For all of the Mexican Pacific (Oct 2026):
# CANNOT BE FRESHWATER; DEFINITE MARINE                   DEFINITE FRESHWATER                         LIKELY MARINE 
#                               5231267                                671082                                571740 
#                NOT FLAGGED EITHER WAY         POSSIBLY FRESHWATER OR MARINE 
#                                 12300                                198253 
                       
# For all of the Mexican Pacific (May 2026):
 # CANNOT BE FRESHWATER; MARINE                 LIKELY MARINE        NOT FLAGGED EITHER WAY POSSIBLY FRESHWATER OR MARINE 
 #                      4915884                        646040                          1261                        181425 
 #               YES FRESHWATER 
 #                       661693 
```

# > STEP 9: Estimate SECTOR based on record details, estimated genera, estimated Major Functional Group, aquaculture flags, and freshwater flags. ------------------------------

```{r Create sector_estimate_reported column}
colnames(Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted)

Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted <- Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted %>%
  mutate(
    sector_estimate_reported = case_when(
      
      # More specific first
      reported_aquaculture_production == "yes" & reported_fleet == "small_scale" ~ "small-scale aquaculture",
      
      # General aquaculture
      reported_aquaculture_production == "yes" ~ "aquaculture",
      
      # Fisheries by fleet
      reported_fleet == "small_scale" ~ "small-scale fisheries",
      reported_fleet == "large_scale" ~ "large-scale fisheries",
      
      # Fallback for missing/unknown
      TRUE ~ "sector details were not reported"
    )
  )
# 6684642 obs., 53 vars.


# SANITY CHECK:
table(Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted$sector_estimate_reported)

# Re-level

    sector_estimate_reported = factor(
      sector_estimate_reported,

        "small-scale fisheries",
        "large-scale fisheries"
      )

  )
```

```{r Create sector_estimate_draft column based on flags}

#### ESTIMATE MOST LIKELY SECTOR based on report info and flags: ####

Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted <- Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted %>%
  mutate(
    # Helper columns
    is_aquaculture = est_aquaculture_production %in% c("aquaculture", "likely aquaculture"),
    is_likely.wildcatch = est_aquaculture_production %in% c("unlikely aquaculture", "not aquaculture", "possibly aquaculture"),
    is_freshwater = freshwater_flag %in% c("DEFINITE FRESHWATER"),
    is_marine.likely = freshwater_flag %in% c("CANNOT BE FRESHWATER; DEFINITE MARINE", "LIKELY MARINE"),
    is_fresh.or.marine = freshwater_flag %in% c("POSSIBLY FRESHWATER OR MARINE", "NOT FLAGGED EITHER WAY"),
    
    # Implement logic to estimate sector
    sector_estimate_draft = case_when(
      
      #### DEFINITE FRESHWATER SECTORS: ####
      is_freshwater & is_aquaculture ~ "freshwater: aquaculture",
      is_freshwater & is_likely.wildcatch & reported_fleet == "small_scale" ~ "freshwater: small-scale capture",
      is_freshwater & is_likely.wildcatch & reported_fleet == "large_scale" ~ "freshwater: large-scale capture",
      is_freshwater ~ "freshwater: fishery sector yet to be classified",
      
      #### DEFINITE & LIKELY MARINE SECTORS: ####
      is_marine.likely & is_aquaculture ~ "marine: aquaculture",
      is_marine.likely & is_likely.wildcatch & reported_fleet == "small_scale" ~ "marine: small-scale capture",
      is_marine.likely & is_likely.wildcatch & reported_fleet == "large_scale" ~ "marine: large-scale capture",
      is_marine.likely ~ "marine: fishery sector yet to be classified",
      
      #### SECTOR UNCERTAIN, COULD GO EITHER WAY: ####
      is_fresh.or.marine & is_aquaculture ~ 
        "freshwater or marine: aquaculture",
      is_fresh.or.marine & is_likely.wildcatch & reported_fleet == "small_scale" ~ 
        "freshwater or marine: small-scale capture",
      is_fresh.or.marine & is_likely.wildcatch & reported_fleet == "large_scale" ~ 
        "freshwater or marine: large-scale capture",
      is_fresh.or.marine ~ 
        "freshwater or marine: fishery sector yet to be classified",
      
      # Catch-all safeguard
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-is_aquaculture, -is_likely.wildcatch, -is_freshwater, -is_marine.likely, -is_fresh.or.marine)


# SANITY CHECK:
table(Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted$sector_estimate_draft)
```

```{r Summarize by sector}
# Reported landings by sector:
Reported.Sector_summary<- Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted %>% 
  filter(year >= 2014, year <= 2025) %>%
  select(year, sector_estimate_reported, weight_kg_corrected, value) %>%
  group_by(year, sector_estimate_reported) %>%
  summarize(est_annual_catch_kg= sum(weight_kg_corrected, na.rm = TRUE),
            est_annual_catch_mt = est_annual_catch_kg/1000,
            est_annual_value= sum(value, na.rm = TRUE))

table(Reported.Sector_summary$sector_estimate_reported)

# Estimated landings by sector:
Est.Sector_summary <- Mex.Pacific_Landings_sorted %>% 
  filter(year >= 2014, year <= 2025) %>%
  select(year, weight_kg_corrected, value, sector_estimate_draft) %>%
  
  group_by(year, sector_estimate_draft) %>%
  summarize(
    est_annual_catch_kg = sum(weight_kg_corrected, na.rm = TRUE),
    est_annual_value    = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # Convert to metric tons
  mutate(est_annual_catch_mt = est_annual_catch_kg / 1000) %>%
  # Compute percent of annual total catch
  
  group_by(year) %>%
  mutate(percent_AnnualTotCatch = round(100 * est_annual_catch_kg / sum(est_annual_catch_kg, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  ungroup()

# Okay great. So from this we can see that the following sectors make up only 0-1% of total catch. I feel comfortable ignoring them then for the purposing of assessing food provising (maybe a different story for natural products) - Mar 24 2026.

# freshwater: large-scale capture
# freshwater: fishery sector yet to be classified
# freshwater or marine: aquaculture
# freshwater or marine: small-scale capture
# freshwater or marine: large-scale capture
# freshwater or marine: fishery sector yet to be classified

table(Est.Sector_summary$sector_estimate_draft)
```

```{r Plot each sector of interest over time}
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey85"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 13, color = "grey30")

  # Optional: better legend layout
  guides(

  )
```

```{r Force of consistency in Nayarit Sonora and Sinaloa}
colnames(NW.Mex_Landings_georeferenced0)

NW.Mex_Landings_georeferenced0 <- NW.Mex_Landings_georeferenced0 %>%

                   "SONORA",
                   "NAYARIT") ~ "yes",
      
      # Otherwise keep existing value
      TRUE ~ GOC_est

    GOC_Include_Exclude = case_when(
      
      # CASE 1: States automatically assigned to the GOC:
      state %in% c("SINALOA", 
                   "SONORA",
                   "NAYARIT") ~ "include",
      
      # Otherwise keep existing value
      TRUE ~ GOC_Include_Exclude
    ),
    
    OHI_region_est = case_when(
      
      state == "SINALOA" ~ "Region_8",
      state == "NAYARIT" ~ "Region_9",
      
      # Otherwise keep existing value
      TRUE ~ OHI_region_est
    ),
    
    OHI_region_name = case_when(
      
      state == "SINALOA" ~ "Sinaloan_Coast",
      state == "NAYARIT" ~ "Nayarit_Jalisco",
      
      # Otherwise keep existing value
      TRUE ~ OHI_region_name
    )
    
  )
```

# PATCH 6 - Records where landing_site is missing.
Assigned these offices manually.
I think this is patched using the final lat-long key. Not sure this patch is necessary, but I'll keep it for now. - Oct, 2026

```{r MANUAL PATCH for Pacific side landing sites}
colnames(NW.Mex_Landings_georeferenced0)

Office_Names <- NW.Mex_Landings_georeferenced0 %>%
  select(state, office_name_clean, landing_site_clean, GOC_Include_Exclude, OHI_region_est) %>%
  filter(is.na(landing_site_clean) & !is.na(office_name_clean)) %>%
  distinct()
# 49 offices where is.na(landing_site), but only a few were region is missing.

# Exported these sites, filled them in manually.
```

```{r Create OfficeRegion_PATCH}
# write.csv(Office_Names,
#          "/home/ferrer/ohi_goc_prep/FP/v2026/CONAPESCA_Keys/Spatial_Keys/PATCH_LatLong_MissingOfficeNames_Oct272026.csv",
#          row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r Load in OfficeRegion_PATCH}
OfficeRegion_PATCH<- read_csv("/home/ferrer/ohi_goc_prep/FP/v2026/CONAPESCA_Keys/Spatial_Keys/PATCH_OfficeRegion_Oct272026.csv")
# 49 obs., 5 vars.

OfficeRegion_PATCH<- OfficeRegion_PATCH %>%
  rename(
    landing_site_clean= landing_site,
    office_name_clean= office_name
  )
```

```{r Apply manual patch}
# The logic is as follows: In cases where landing_site is NA, use the OfficeRegion_PATCH to update the inside_GOC column.

# Clean and standardize both tables:
NW.Mex_Landings_georeferenced0 <- NW.Mex_Landings_georeferenced0 %>%
  mutate(
    state_clean = str_to_upper(str_trim(stri_trans_general(state, "Latin-ASCII"))),
    landing_site_na = is.na(landing_site_clean) | landing_site_clean == ""  # treat empty strings as missing
  )
# 4944027 obs., 67 vars.

OfficeRegion_PATCH <- OfficeRegion_PATCH %>%
  mutate(
    state_clean = str_to_upper(str_trim(stri_trans_general(state, "Latin-ASCII"))),
  )

# Apply patch only where landing_site is NA:
# Split NW.Mex_Landings_georeferenced0 into rows WITH and WITHOUT landing_site:
with_site <- NW.Mex_Landings_georeferenced0 %>%
  filter(!landing_site_na)

without_site <- NW.Mex_Landings_georeferenced0 %>%
  filter(landing_site_na)

# Strict join using state + office + landing_site:
Landings_with_site <- with_site %>%
  left_join(OfficeRegion_PATCH,
            by = c("state_clean", 
                   "office_name_clean", 
                   "landing_site_clean"),
            suffix = c("", "_patch")) %>%
  mutate(GOC_Include_Exclude = coalesce(GOC_Include_Exclude, GOC_Include_Exclude),
         OHI_region_est = coalesce(OHI_region_est, OHI_region_est)) %>%
  select(-GOC_Include_Exclude_patch, -OHI_region_est_patch)

# Relaxed join using state + office only:
Landings_without_site <- without_site %>%
  left_join(OfficeRegion_PATCH %>% select(-landing_site_clean),
            by = c("state_clean", 
                   "office_name_clean"),
            suffix = c("", "_patch")) %>%
  mutate(GOC_Include_Exclude = coalesce(GOC_Include_Exclude, GOC_Include_Exclude),
         OHI_region_est = coalesce(OHI_region_est, OHI_region_est)) %>%
  select(-GOC_Include_Exclude_patch, -OHI_region_est_patch)

# Recombine:
NW.Mex_Landings_georef_patched <- bind_rows(Landings_with_site, Landings_without_site)

dim(NW.Mex_Landings_georef_patched)
# 4944027 obs., 68 vars. (as expected)

```

```{r SANITY CHECKS: Did the patch work as expected?}

table(NW.Mex_Landings_georeferenced0$GOC_Include_Exclude)

# 1284584 3659108
table(NW.Mex_Landings_georef_patched$GOC_Include_Exclude)

# 1284584 3659108 

table(NW.Mex_Landings_georeferenced0$OHI_region_est)
# Region_1 Region_2 Region_3 Region_4 Region_5 Region_6 Region_7 Region_8 Region_9 
#    58062    91986   180085   355082   177185   113135   374189  1445270   857897 
table(NW.Mex_Landings_georef_patched$OHI_region_est)
# Region_1 Region_2 Region_3 Region_4 Region_5 Region_6 Region_7 Region_8 Region_9 
#    58062    91986   180085   355082   177185   113135   374189  1445270   857897

# Any empties left?
```
